blocks.text:
The **quickstart and factory-test kit** for the board: known-good bitstreams to check a
new board, set up the FT231X and ESP32, install bootloaders, and try demos. It is also a
**catalogue of the earliest designs people ran on the ULX3S**. Each folder points
to a source project.

sections.title: Contents (one bullet per folder, `fpga/…` unless stated)

rows.Function tags: soc-cpu, video-dvi, rtc-power, adc, audio-dac, examples
rows.What it is: **Board self-test**: f32c MIPS/RISC-V SoC plus `selftest-mcp7940n.bin`. Checks RTC, EDID, ADC, DAC, buttons, switches and LEDs, and prints results on serial and DVI. Also BASIC, galaga, a synth and a slides viewer
USB-serial → ESP32 bridge for flashing the ESP32, per revision and chip
**Recommended bootloader**: DFU on US2 plus ESP32 passthru on US1, multiboot `.img` (12F/25F/45F/85F on v20, v314, v317; ULX4M)
Older TinyFPGA-style US2 bootloader, 2018
SDRAM memory test at 112–210 MHz with various clock phases (32/64 MB), 2019
SDRAM memtest EMI variant for v3.1.7, 2021
OLED + button test (25F/45F), 2018
RTC clock shown on DVI + ST7789, set with buttons
USB1.0 low-speed HID host on US2, shows reports as hex
LAN8720 RMII on GP/GN 9–13; hdl4fpga DHCP + ping responder

rows.Function tags: adc, video-dvi, oled-lcd, ps2, usb-device, ethernet
rows.What it is: **4-channel storage oscilloscope** with mouse GUI on 800×600 or OLED; USB CDC-Ethernet on US2
Graphics slides viewer fed from ESP32 MicroPython
Commodore 64 (free ROMs) for 12F/85F, PRG loader + OSD over ESP32
Project Oberon RISC5 workstation (12F, 85F; cache edition from PNRU)
**Linux on LiteX/VexRiscv**, 50 MHz, framebuffer on GPDI, rootfs on SD
Probe flash pins with a wire from GP27 to check BGA soldering
Scripts to run Lattice Diamond on Debian/Ubuntu
esptool/espefuse, efuse burn script, websvf binaries, MicroPython v1.14 + esp32ecp5, RTC demo
ujprog, FleaFPGA-JTAG, OpenOCD, ftx_prog binaries for Linux/RPi/Win/macOS
Gerbers for PCB v3.1.3

blocks.text: "unknown" = the source is not stated in the repo; guesses are marked with `?`.

Board bring-up: program the FT231X with `ftx_prog`, load
`f32c/…selftest…bit`, upload `f32c-bin/selftest-mcp7940n.bin` with `f32cup.py`, then read
serial at 115200 or the DVI screen. After that: passthru to flash, burn the ESP32 efuse
(3.3 V flash, WROOM only), upload websvf.

DFU bootloader install:
`openFPGALoader -b ulx3s --unprotect-flash --file-type bin -f multiboot.img.gz`.
Enter it by holding BTN1 while plugging US2 (LEDs D0–D2 on).

items:
Best known-good bitstreams for **checking hardware** before debugging your own design
(self-test, memtest, flashblink).

`memtest/` file names give a reference for how fast SDRAM runs on ULX3S (up to ~200 MHz
with a tuned clock phase). Pass/fail results are not recorded in the repo.
**hdl4fpga** (scope, eth, slides) is a major reusable-core source: DVI, RMII, USB CDC-ECM, PS/2. Review it.

The README's hardware bring-up notes (diode test of BGA pins, regulator jumpers RP1–3,
< 50 mA idle current) are useful for anyone assembling boards.
Sources for memtest, emi, oled, rtc, usb, c64, oberon, flashblink need to be located.
